item.title: [ZEPPELIN-2758] NumberFormatException on importing notebook
item.description:
Regression from https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/ZEPPELIN-2397

Steps to replicate:

  1. Build Zeppelin (latest master - ad3138385350e62 - mvn clean package -DskipTests)
  2. Open notebook "Zeppelin Tutorial/Basic Features (Spark)"
  3. Export notebook
  4. Go to main page > Import note
  5. "Select JSON File" > Select prev exported file > Exception thrown

Thanks zjffdu! really appreciated if you can help as I'm not an expert on this at all.

I'll share what I attempted so far.

*First *
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11586299/how-to-prevent-gson-from-converting-a-long-number-a-json-string-to-scientific
tried to use LongSerializationPolicy.STRING here:
.setLongSerializationPolicy(LongSerializationPolicy.STRING)
https://github.com/nokia/zeppelin/blob/master/zeppelin-zengine/src/main/java/org/apache/zeppelin/notebook/Note.java#L64
This had no effect on the json file export/import.

*Second *
http://java.qahowto.com/How-to-handle-a-NumberFormatException-with-Gson-in-deserialization-a-JSON-response-java-json-deserialization-gson-873ec5
tried to create a custom "long" class as per example above and register it

.registerTypeAdapter(LongRuntime.class, new NotebookImportLongDeserializer())

public class LongRuntime {
  private long value;

  public LongRuntime(long runtime) {
    this.value = runtime;
  }

  public long getValue() {
    return value;
  }
}

public class NotebookImportLongDeserializer implements JsonDeserializer<LongRuntime> {

  @Override
  public LongRuntime deserialize(JsonElement jsonElement, Type typeOF,
    JsonDeserializationContext context) throws JsonParseException {
    try {
      if (jsonElement.isJsonObject()) {
        JsonObject obj = jsonElement.getAsJsonObject();
        return new LongRuntime(obj.get("value").getAsLong());
      } else {
        String elem = jsonElement.getAsString();
        if (elem.contains(".")) {
          return new LongRuntime(new Double(jsonElement.getAsDouble()).longValue());
        } else {
          return new LongRuntime(jsonElement.getAsLong());
        }
      }
    } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
      throw new NumberFormatException("Unparsable number: \"" + jsonElement.getAsString());
    }
  }
}

Job.java...
private LongRuntime progressUpdateIntervalMs;

It works but it keeps the property as an object which isn't great

"progressUpdateIntervalMs":{"value":500}

I can get a pull request with my changes but I'm not sure it's the right approach.
Let me know if you find a third, better option, to deal with this issue.
Many thanks zjffdu
